sentences.text: This dinosaur reached a total length of approximately 2.25 meters.
Its skull was quite short, measuring less than two-thirds the length of the femur.
Evidence from its dentition suggests that the animal was primarily a herbivore.
Most of the teeth were lance-shaped with rough surfaces designed for processing vegetation.
These teeth were slightly curved backward and featured a constriction at the base.
The cutting edges possessed relatively large ridges perpendicular to the edge, with three to five denticles per millimeter.
The lower edge of the ilium bone over the hip joint is straight.
The tibia lacks a clear fibular crest.
The second and third premaxillary teeth are the longest in the head, only slightly longer than the fourth and fifth maxillary teeth.
Teeth are missing from the premaxillary and front dentary positions, though it is unclear if this is a fixed morphology or accidental wear.
The animal had approximately fifteen vertebrae that were amphicoelous, meaning hollow at both the front and back.
The preserved tail vertebrae lacked a hypophene-hypantrum complex.
Bagualosaurus was the largest known sauropodomorph of the Carnian period, before later sauropodomorphs gradually increased in size.
The holotype skeleton was found in a rare position with the animal lying on its back and hindlimbs pulled up.
A sauropodomorph skeleton was excavated in 2007 from a ravine near Agudo in Rio Grande do Sul.
The skeleton was discovered in 2007 in the Janner rock formation, two kilometers from Agudo in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.
The skeleton was remarkably articulated, a rarity for Triassic fossils, and likely disturbed by invertebrates shortly after the animal's death.
The skeleton was found lying on its back with both hind legs raised, an unusual posture for archosaur fossils.
The species Bagualosaurus agudoensis was named and described in 2018 by Pretto, Langer, and Schultz.
While retaining powerful hind legs suited for running, the animal shows clear adaptations for a herbivorous lifestyle in its smaller skull and teeth.
The animal likely had a mixed diet or shifted to herbivory, indicated by its powerful legs for speed alongside smaller skull and teeth adaptations for plant eating.
Bagualosaurus is classified as a dinosaur in the order Saurischia and suborder Sauropodomorpha.
Bagualosaurus is a genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur.
Bagualosaurus is classified in a derived position within Sauropodomorpha, placed below Pantydraco and above the clade containing Chromogisaurus and Saturnalia.
Bagualosaurus lived approximately 230 million years ago during the Carnian stage of the Late Triassic period.
Fossils of Bagualosaurus were found in the Candelária Sequence (Uppermost Santa Maria Formation) of Brazil.
The genus lived from the Carnian to the Norian stages, between 237 and 205.7 million years ago.
